step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture shows an automated, event-driven batch processing workflow for regulatory compliance files. 1. Customers upload files to an S3 Uploads Bucket, which sends event notifications to an SQS queue. 2. A CloudWatch scheduled event triggers a Queue Checker Lambda function every 5 minutes. The Lambda checks the SQS queue for new jobs and triggers Step Functions. 3. Step Functions invokes an Intermediate Lambda function to launch a dedicated Windows EC2 instance for batch processing. The EC2 instance retrieves software setup/configuration from an S3 Config Bucket, reports task execution status back to Step Functions, and stores batch execution outputs into an RDS (SQL Server) database.

graph.name: FICO Serverless & On-Demand Batch Processing Architecture
graph.notes: FICO's batch workflow uses S3, SQS, CloudWatch, Lambda, Step Functions, EC2 (Windows), and SQL Server (RDS) to perform compliance checks on customer uploaded transaction files.
